title: Pluggable Scan Advisor and Query Surface Cache Coordinator to reduce dashboard scan latency
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Several dashboard queries for usage analytics frequently trigger wide scans across hot and cold partitions, resulting in high read amplification and long tail latencies (p95/p99). Current ad-hoc fixes (per-query TTL tweaks, local microcaches) have reduced pain for a few endpoints but add operational complexity and duplicated cache state across services.

Problem: We need a coordinated, low-risk way to: (1) identify which queries should use index hints or materialized snapshots vs scanned paths; (2) consolidate cache ownership for the top-of-surface dashboard queries so evictions and TTLs are consistent; (3) make runtime routing decisions cheaply so we do not add significant overhead to the request path.

Goal: Build a pluggable Scan Advisor service (offline analysis + lightweight runtime API) and a Query Surface Cache Coordinator that centralizes TTL/eviction policies for surface-level dashboard caches. Success criteria: reduce dashboard p95 latency by 25% for affected widgets, decrease dashboard read IO by 30% for experiments, and keep additional CPU overhead under 5% at median request rate.

Scope: MVP focuses on the Console usage analytics dashboard endpoints (per-tenant topk lists, time-windowed aggregations, and ad-hoc exploration queries used by the product team). This work does NOT include full materialized view infra or rearchitecting the underlying index formats. We will provide advisory hints + short-lived snapshotting and a shared caching layer for surface queries.

Proposed design:
1) Offline analyzer: a periodic job that fingerprints query shapes and computes heuristics: scan width estimate, selective index-compatibility score, historical cardinality, and cacheability score. Runs in the analytics cluster and writes per-query advisories to the config store.
2) Scan Advisor API: lightweight HTTP/gRPC endpoint consulted by the dashboard query router. Returns one of: {prefer-index, prefer-snapshot, prefer-scan, prefer-snapshot-with-ttl, force-cache-key=K}. Responses are cached locally for 5m to avoid adding latency.
3) Query Surface Cache Coordinator: a central service that maintains canonical cache keys for common dashboard surfaces (widget+params+tenant fingerprint) and drives eviction policies (LRU with tenant fairness buckets and dynamic TTL hints). Integrates with existing in-memory LRU caches and Redis clusters; serves as authoritative leader for TTLs and shard ownership to prevent duplicate caching with conflicting TTLs.
4) Runtime router changes: the dashboard query router calls Scan Advisor (fast cache) to decide execution strategy. If advisor returns prefer-snapshot/force-cache-key, the router queries the Cache Coordinator to fetch or populate snapshot atomically. Fall back to existing scan path on cache miss with async warm-up.

Tradeoffs and constraints: advisor introduces extra coordination but keeps changes out of core storage engine. Snapshotting adds write/space overhead; we will cap snapshot retention and use delta snapshots for large ranges. Centralized coordinator reduces duplication but is a single logical component (we will make it horizontally scalable and partitioned by tenant namespace).

Testing and metrics: we will add the following dashboards and alerts: cache hit ratio by surface, advisor decision distribution, per-strategy p50/p95/p99 latencies, read IO reduction per tenant, coordinator error rate. Benchmarks: run synthetic workloads replaying 7 days of production traffic to estimate savings before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor exposes a fast runtime API with cached responses and <2ms median added latency
Coordinator centralizes TTL configuration and prevents duplicate cache entries for top 50 surfaces
End-to-end experiment shows >=25% p95 reduction on at least 3 representative dashboard widgets
Canary rollout plan with automated rollback on error rate spike or p95 regression
Documentation and runbook created with operator steps and metrics to monitor
decisions: Use heuristic offline analyzer first; defer ML-based advisor to a follow-up cycle
Coordinator will use namespaced keys (tenant+surface+params hash) and integrate with existing Redis clusters rather than adding a new datastore
Snapshots will be short-lived (default 10m) with option to extend based on advisory score
Advisor responses are advisory only; any forced changes will use staged rollout and observability gating
